title: Type-Balanced Contextual Learning for Incremental Named Entity Recognition
abstract: arXiv:2608.31038v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Incremental Named Entity Recognition (INER) stands as a pivotal task in information extraction, emphasizing the successive identification of new entity types within unstructured text. Faced with the continuous influx of entity types, INER grapples with two significant challenges: the widespread issue of catastrophic forgetting and the unique shift issue of the non-entity type semantics. While pseudo-labeling-based INER methods have proven effective in addressing these challenges, a previously overlooked issue arises: the biased context problem. Our analysis shows that, in new sentences, the contextual associations of tokens representing old entity types exhibit a significantly stronger bias towards new entity types compared to their contexts in old sentences. translated_title: 面向增量命名实体识别的类型平衡上下文学习
translated_abstract: 增量命名实体识别（INER）是信息抽取中的一项关键任务，其重点在于在非结构化文本中持续识别新的实体类型。面对不断涌现的实体类型，INER面临两大显著挑战：普遍存在的灾难性遗忘问题，以及非实体类型语义的独特漂移问题。尽管基于伪标签的INER方法已被证明能有效应对这些挑战，但一个此前被忽视的问题随之浮现：有偏上下文问题。我们的分析表明，在新句子中，代表旧实体类型的词元其上下文关联相比它们在旧句子中的上下文，对新实体类型表现出显著更强的偏向。这种倾向加剧了旧知识的退化，同时助长了新知识的过拟合。为解决这一有偏上下文问题，我们提出了一种类型平衡上下文学习器（Type-Balanced Contextual Learner）。
tldr: 本文发现了增量命名实体识别中此前被忽视的有偏上下文问题，即新句子中旧实体类型词元的上下文显著偏向新实体类型，并据此提出类型平衡上下文学习方法，以缓解旧知识退化和新知识过拟合。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies a previously overlooked biased context problem in incremental named entity recognition, where the contexts of old entity type tokens in new sentences are significantly biased toward new entity types, and proposes a Type-Balanced Contextual Learning approach to mitigate old knowledge degradation and new knowledge overfitting.
